title: Tight Hoeffding bound on the exponential loss
statement:
Let $p_1,\dots,p_n$ be a probability distribution, so $p_i \ge 0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n p_i = 1$, and let $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n \in [0,1]$ be losses. Write $L = \sum_{i=1}^n p_i\,\ell_i$ for the expected loss. Then for every $\eta > 0$,
\[
  \log\!\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\,e^{-\eta\,\ell_i}\Bigr)
  \;\le\;
  -\eta\,L + \frac{\eta^2}{8}.
\]
replaced:
Under the same hypotheses as \texttt{hoeffding\_log\_mgf\_weak}, the tighter bound holds:
\[
  \ln\!\Bigl(\sum_{i} p_i\,e^{-\eta\,\ell_i}\Bigr)
  \;\le\;
  -\eta L + \frac{\eta^2}{8}.
\]
